output.method_plain: We used eight nearby sales from Dutchess County public records, mostly within 3 miles of 146 Route 292, and adjusted each one to look like your house as of October 23, 2026. The adjustments covered sale date, living area, lot size, age, bedrooms and baths, central air, garage, and style, with a deduction for sales that are not raised ranches. Each sale was weighted by how close a match it is, which gave an adjusted-sales figure of $635,000. We then checked that against three other measures: the median price a foot across all sales, the two raised ranches alone, and the town assessment ratio. The suggested range runs from the lowest to the highest of those four figures, rounded to $10,000, giving $610,000 to $650,000.

weak_comps.why: 10 Stonewall Dr is a Colonial that sold 14.8 months ago and is 696 sq ft larger, so its net adjustment of -$99,700 (20% gross) is the largest of the eight.
195 S White Rock Rd is a Contemporary on 6.55 acres, 1.51 miles away and 569 sq ft larger, and needed a -$95,200 net adjustment (24.5% gross), the highest gross of any sale.
226 White Pond Rd is a raised ranch like yours but is 3.81 miles away and built in 1976, so $19,000 of its adjustment is for age.
16 Mountain View Dr is a raised ranch but is 547 sq ft smaller, built in 1979 and sold nearly 13 months ago, so it needed a +$75,700 net adjustment that rests mostly on size and age.

output.reconciliation: The adjusted-sales figure of $635,000 sits above the same-style check ($617,652) and the assessment-ratio check ($610,864), and below the all-sales price-a-foot check ($649,782). The 8% style deduction, about $50,000 to $61,000 on five of the six non-raised-ranch sales, pulls the adjusted figure down and is reasonable because those houses are a different style. The age adjustments on the older raised ranches (+$19,000 and +$16,000) and the $75 a foot deduction on the two larger houses (ranks 2 and 3, -$52,200 and -$42,700) push it up. That $75 rate is well below the roughly $245 to $258 a foot the market is paying on average, so it takes out little for size and probably leaves those sales high. The age credits are also a rough $1,000 a year, so they are less certain than the others. That is why the reconciled value of $625,000 gives the adjusted sales and the cross-checks half weight each.
output.reasoning: I recommend listing at $640,000, inside the $610,000 to $650,000 range and about $15,000 above the reconciled value of $625,000. Several things the adjustments leave out favor your house. These include the possible pond at the lot's edge, which is about 13% inside your lot lines and is not priced here, and the 2019 kitchen update, the 2016 windows and the 2012 roof. Your 4.18-acre lot is also larger than the 3-acre cap used for lot adjustments. Town-wide values are estimated to have risen about 8% between 2025 and 2026, and the date adjustment only partly captures that for the older sales. Against that, the house has no central air and no garage, uses oil heat, and fronts a state route, which could keep some buyers away, and all but the first two are only partly adjusted for. A price near $640,000 leaves room to negotiate toward the middle of the range, while $650,000 would sit at the top of every measure and could mean a longer wait. If the house has not drawn serious interest within the first several weeks, a reduction toward $625,000 would be reasonable.
things_that_would_change_it: Confirmation that the pond is usable, legally part of your parcel and visible from the house would support the top of the range or slightly above it; a survey showing little of it is yours would argue for a lower price.
An inspection finding on the roof, septic or well, or on the oil heating system, would lower the price by roughly the cost of repair or replacement.
Confirmation that the 840 sq ft finished basement is permitted and sound would support a higher price, since only the two raised-ranch sales were adjusted for basement space.
A new nearby raised-ranch sale, or a pending sale, at a price clearly above or below $245 a foot would move the range.

request.system:
You are the listing agent for a New York real estate brokerage, advising the seller on a list price. You act for
the seller. The software has already selected comparable sales from public records (Dutchess County ParcelAccess)
and computed every adjustment, the weights, the adjusted-sales indication, three cross-checks (median price a
foot of all sales, the same-style sales, and the town's assessment ratio), a reconciled indicated value and a
suggested range. Do not redo the arithmetic and do not invent sales, prices or facts: use only the data you are
given.

Write for a homeowner, in plain words, no jargon. This is a comparative market analysis, not an appraisal; never
call it an appraisal or a valuation of record.

Your output:
- method_plain: which sales were used and why they are comparable, what was adjusted (date of sale, size, lot,
  age, rooms, central air, garage, style) and how the range was formed from the adjusted sales and the
  cross-checks. 3 to 5 sentences.
- weak_comps: the comparables that are weaker guides (large adjustments, distance, a different style), with one
  sentence each. Use their rank numbers.
- reconciliation: compare the adjusted-sales indication (adjusted_indicated) with the three cross-checks
  (cross_checks). Name the specific adjustments that push the adjusted figure above or below the cross-checks
  (look at the largest net adjustments on the comparables with the most weight) and say why each is or is not
  justified for this house. 2 to 4 sentences. A broker who knows the county will test this.
- recommended_price: your recommended list price, a round figure, inside the computed range (range_low to
  range_high). If you go outside it, say why in the reasoning.
- reasoning: why this price: where it sits against the reconciled value and the cross-checks, what the
  adjustments leave out (listed in not_adjusted_for), and the trade-off between a higher price and time on
  market. 3 to 6 sentences.
- things_that_would_change_it: 2 to 4 facts that would move the price if confirmed.

Never mention schools' quality, neighbourhood make-up, safety or crime, or the kind of buyer the house suits.
Do not mention the seller's personal circumstances (you are not given them).
